# Bernoulli Design

## Introduction

In the Bernoulli design (BE) the indicator variables are iid:

$$I_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\pi)  \ \ \forall i \in U$$

1. We fix a value of $\pi$.
2. We generate $RN\sim U(0,1) \ \ \forall i \in U$.
3. The sample $s$: the individuals whose $RN\leq \pi$.
4. $P[I_i=1]=\pi$ and $P[I_i=0]=1-\pi$.
5. the sample size is not fixed (i.e. it is random).

## Inclusion probabilities and sample size

- $\pi_i=\pi \ \ \forall i \in U$
- $\pi_{ij}=\pi^2 \ \ \forall i \neq j \in U$
- $\Delta_{ij}=0$

The sample size ($n_s$) is random and follows a binomial distribution:

$$n_s \sim \text{Binomial}(N,\pi) $$

where $E(n_s)=N\pi$ and $V(n_s)=N\pi(1-\pi)$.

## Bernoulli design

If $n_s$ is the (expected) sample size, the BE design can be written as:

$$p(s)=\pi^{n_s}(1-\pi)^{N-n_s}$$

If we approximate the binomial using the CLT:

$$N\pi \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{N\pi(1-\pi)}$$

# Estimation

## HT estimator

The HT estimator for the total of variable $y$ is:

$$\hat Y_{\text{HT}}=\frac{1}{\pi}\sum\limits_{i\in s} y_i=w \sum\limits_{i\in s} y_i $$

The variance of the estimator is:

$$V_{BE}(\hat Y_{\text{HT}})=(\pi^{-1}-1)\sum\limits_{i\in U} y_i^2 $$

And a variance estimator is:

$$\hat {V}_{BE}(\hat Y_{\text{HT}})=\pi^{-1}(\pi^{-1}-1)\sum\limits_{i\in s} y_i^2 $$

## Alternative estimator

Let $n_{exp}=N\pi$ be the expected sample size.

The alternative estimator of $Y$ is given by:

$$ \hat Y_{\text{alt}}=\frac{n_{exp}}{n_s}\hat Y_{\text{HT}}=\frac{N}{n_s}\sum\limits_{i\in s} y_i$$

We can approximate the variance as in SRS:

$$V(\hat Y_{\text{alt}})\approx N^2(1-n_s/N)\,\text{var}_U[y]/n_s $$

Applying the correction $\frac{n_{exp}}{n_s}$ removes variability from the estimator compared to the HT estimator.

## Design effect

The design effect is:

$$ \text{deff}(BE,\hat Y_{HT})=1-\frac{1}{N}+\frac{1}{(\text{cv}_U[y])^2}\approx 1+\frac{1}{(\text{cv}_U[y])^2}$$
